To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of pig farms in Thailand has decreased by more than 50% since 1998.
pig farming is a spatially heterogeneous practice that varies in terms of the number of pig units per farm, and the number of farms in each district.

the spatial analysis of pig farming in the Northeast of Thailand shows a high density of farms, with a large number of small farms, and that the characteristics of the farms are strongly related to the location and to the type of land use in the vicinity of the farm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial distribution of pig farms in Thailand, and their characteristics.
the development of a spatial analysis of pig farming in the central plain of Thailand.
the development of a spatial analysis tool that can be used to identify areas of pig farming activity in Thailand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pig farming in Thailand is a complex system of different production and marketing systems, where the pig production is a part of an extensive and complex farming system.
the pig population in Thailand is not increasing and the pig industry in Thailand is not expanding, and it has not expanded since the mid-1990s.
Thailand is the largest producer of pork and pork products in the world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to develop and test a spatially explicit model for pig farming in Thailand and have been able to show that the model performs well in terms of predicting pig farming at the village level and that the model can be used for policy analysis.
we have been able to identify a spatial pattern for pig farming in Thailand and to characterize the pig farms in terms of size, type, and production.
we have developed an integrated spatial decision support system that allows the identification and evaluation of alternative locations for pig farming.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pig population in Thailand is concentrated in the central region of the country, with the highest densities in Nakhon Sawan, Phichit and Kamphaeng Phet provinces, and in the southern region, with the highest concentrations in Phatthalung, Songkhla and Pattani provinces.
the pig industry in Thailand has been undergoing a transition from backyard to commercial farming.
there are significant differences in pig farming characteristics across Thailand.
